name: Nereus
overview: Nereus is a male individual mentioned in the New Testament to whom the Apostle Paul sends greetings in Romans 16:15. Beyond this brief mention, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal background. His inclusion in Paul's greetings indicates he was a recognized member of the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Nereus is presented as a proper name in Romans 16:15. There is no specific meaning or divine origin noted for this name in the biblical text, and thus it is simply recognized as his given name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Nereus beyond the fact that Paul greets him in Romans 16:15. There are no other relational details provided in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Nereus holds significance as a member of the early church to whom Paul extends greetings, demonstrating the interconnectedness and fellowship among believers in the first-century Christian community. His mention by Paul highlights the personal nature of Paul's ministry and the importance of mutual encouragement among the saints. Although little is known about Nereus beyond this greeting, his inclusion affirms his place within the body of Christ during the formative years of the church.
